children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were a pinch lower Thursday morning, but poised to drop further on pressure from weaker comparable oils.
Crude oil was retreating sharply, with spillover pushing European rapeseed, Malaysian palm oil, plus Chicago soybeans and soyoil to the downside. Chicago soymeal was posting modest increases.
Statistics Canada estimated canola production at 22.05 million metric tons Wednesday, just short of last year's record crop.
However, traders were now looking past the data, focussing on harvest progress.
Saskatchewan will issue its next crop report later Thursday. Last week, the canola harvest was 9% complete, with all crops at 27% done.
The November canola contract remained ahead of its major moving averages, underpinning the oilseed.
Canola crush margins eased back a few dollars with the November positions between C$273.70 to C$292.95 per metric ton above the futures.
The Canadian dollar was lower on Thursday morning with the loonie falling to 71.50 U.S. cents, compared to Wednesday's close of 71.70.
Approximately 15,250 contracts had been traded by 9:49 a.m. EDT and prices in Canadian dollars per metric ton were:

Price      Change

Jan       836.10     dn 1.70 
Mar       844.50     dn 1.90
